title.narrative: Strengthened legislative and policy frameworks for the protection of the rights of all workers including migrants and other marginalized groups

description.narrative: While South Africa has made strides to address child labour, statistical data show that child labourers still exist in the country including its worst forms. The ILO’s Standards Supervisory bodies have requested government to put measures in place to enhance the progressive elimination of child labour. Following the 4th Phase child Labour Programme of Action, South Africa is still to finalize the 5th Phase Child Labour Programme of Action. The Accelerator Lab 8.7 project aims to intensifying the eradication of forced labour and targets the fishing industry in South Africa. Inspections on board some fishing vessels on South Africa’s shores suggest the presence of forced labour in the sector. While South Africa has been the primary destination for intra-SADC migrants and from across the African continent and further afield, it still does not have a National Labour Migration Policy. There is also need for further support to programmes and policies responsive to population groups in situations of vulnerability such as women, persons with disability, the LGBTQI community, particularly in the HIV/AIDS/TB management programmes, and in the just transition, and inclusion in climate action. The strategy will focus on capacity, technical and policy advisory support for the drafting of the 5th Phase Child Labour Programme of Action designed in the framework of the Durban Call to Action; towards the finalization of the National Labour Migration Policy; towards policy interventions to deal with the elimination of forced labour in South Africa’s fishing industry; and capacity support towards policy interventions in the management of HIV/AIDS/TB responsive to the principles of inclusivity, and non-discrimination; and policy measures that factor in gender in climate action and the just transition to a greener economy.
